item.title: Dify 1.19.0 推出巢狀工作流程追蹤，強化 App 套件、Skills 與 Agent 檔案管理
item.itunes:title: Dify 1.19.0 推出巢狀工作流程追蹤，強化 App 套件、Skills 與 Agent 檔案管理
item.itunes:author: laipz8200
item.itunes:summary:
Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools. Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree.

This release also makes Workflow Tools portable with App packages, adds Skill Hub automation, and makes Agent files easier to upload and preview. The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to 0.6.14-local.

Release highlights · Upgrade guide · Detailed changes

Release highlights

Nested workflow tracing

See what happens inside a Workflow Tool, all the way down to its LLM calls.

Building on the Console drilldown introduced in 1.18.0, new external traces now include the persisted execution steps inside called Workflow Tools. Child steps appear beneath the Tool span that invoked them, preserving the hierarchy across nested and repeated calls. (#44673)

From the outer workflow to a nested LLM call: the execution tree and formatted messages, together in Langfuse. Screenshot from #44673.

  • Follow the hierarchy. Expand called Workflow Tools to see their internal execution steps under the invoking Tool span.
  • Understand each invocation. Repeated calls and failures retain their place in the trace.
  • Keep the LLM context. Inspect formatted prompts and responses, token usage, and project, trace, and observation links.

Note

Your saved provider settings continue to work. The richer hierarchy applies to new executions; historical traces are not backfilled. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. For rolling deployments, follow the tracing queue transition below.

Take Workflow Tools with your apps

Export an app and bring the workflows behind its Workflow Tools with it. .ifpkg packages include those workflows at their bound versions, including transitive dependencies. Import reuses tools already in the destination workspace and recreates, publishes, and registers missing ones, remapping their references. (#44592)

All Dify app exports now use package format v2, including apps without Workflow Tools. Existing v1 imports and explicit YAML export remain supported. See the upgrade guide before importing new packages into older installations. (#45353)

Upload together. Preview in place.

Select or drop multiple Agent configuration files and upload them in parallel. Successful uploads are bound in one atomic batch, concurrent Composer saves preserve the latest files, and Prompt uploads keep the cursor position while inserting multiple references. (#44947)

Read PDFs inline, inspect source files with syntax highlighting, and see when text has been truncated. Previews cover configured files, Skill members, and working-directory files, with a download action when a PDF cannot be loaded. (#45032, #45045)

See Agent file uploads and previews

Read a PDF directly in the Agent file preview and switch between project files.

Select several files and upload them together.

Inspect source files with syntax highlighting and line numbers.

Developer spotlight

Manage workspace Skills through OpenAPI and difyctl. Find and inspect Skills, export a draft or published version, import local files, and publish a new version from the command line. (#44941)

The six Skill commands
Command Capability
difyctl get skill List Skills, with keyword and tag filters.
difyctl describe skill Read details, the draft hash, and latest published version.
difyctl get skill version List published versions.
difyctl export skill Export the draft or a selected published version as ZIP.
difyctl import skill --files <dir> Create a Skill or replace an existing Skill's draft from local files.
difyctl publish skill Publish the draft as a new version.

These operations require an account caller, the corresponding workspace permissions, and Skills to be enabled. Import does not publish. Importing over an existing Skill is classified as destructive; the operation catalog and CLI help distinguish read, write, and destructive operations. (#44941, #45314, #44587)

Upgrade guide

Important

Read the upgrade guide before deploying. Docker Compose now requires v2.35.0 or later. Preserve existing environment files, upgrade the Dify components together, and use the new tracing queue during rolling deployments. New App packages use format v2 and require a compatible destination importer. The bundled plugin daemon moves to 0.6.14-local.

Compatibility and rollout

  1. Back up first. Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, deployment secrets, and environment files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade.
  2. Upgrade the components together. Use matching 1.19.0 API, worker, web, Agent Backend, and Local sandbox images, with plugin daemon 0.6.14-local. Keep the existing Local sandbox authentication token and any configured PASSWORD_PEPPER unchanged. If upgrading from before 1.18.0, also follow the 1.18.0 upgrade guide.
  3. Use Docker Compose 2.35.0 or later. This is the minimum supported version for root .env overrides to take precedence when Compose resolves service defaults. Check your installed version with docker compose version. (#45359)
  4. Keep tracked defaults separate from local overrides. Bundled docker/envs/**/*.defaults files load automatically. Customize a service through its matching local .env file, using the override path documented in the defaults file; root docker/.env holds deployment inputs and explicit overrides. Preserve existing .env files and edit them in place. Review accidentally empty assignments and values pinned by older template copies before upgrading. (#45359, #45376)
  5. Existing shared.env files remain supported. Common API, worker, and Beat customizations now belong in docker/envs/core-services/api-worker.env. Compose still reads legacy docker/envs/core-services/shared.env first, then api-worker.env, so api-worker.env wins when both set conflicting values. Root docker/.env takes precedence over both. An unchanged copy of api-worker.defaults preserves existing shared.env customizations. See the Docker configuration guide. (#45376)
  6. Separate tracing queues during a rolling upgrade. New tasks default to OPS_TRACE_QUEUE=ops_trace_v2; API, workers, and Beat must agree. Custom CELERY_QUEUES, CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES, or --queues lists must include the new queue. Keep old tracing workers on ops_trace until old producers and all their queued, active, reserved, scheduled, and retry work have finished. Do not purge the old queue or ask the new retired handler to export legacy messages. See the tracing rollout guide. (#44673)
  7. Upgrade package destinations before importing new App packages. New app packages always use format v2. Older importers, including builds with the earlier strict v2 rule, may reject them. Version 1 imports remain supported on 1.19.0. Explicit YAML export remains available, but does not carry bundled Workflow Tool dependencies. (#44592, #45353)
Deployment instructions · Docker Compose, source, and difyctl

Docker Compose

Once the 1.19.0 release tag and images are published, stop a single-stack deployment gracefully, switch to the release, retain and review configuration, then pull and start the new images:

cd dify/docker
docker compose stop -t -1
git fetch --tags
git checkout 1.19.0
# Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here.
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Keep API startup migrations enabled (MIGRATION_ENABLED=true), or apply the full migration chain through your managed migration process before starting new workers. For rolling deployments, follow the separate tracing-queue sequence instead of mixing old and new consumers.

Configure shared plugin credentials, PLUGIN_DAEMON_KEY and PLUGIN_DIFY_INNER_API_KEY, in root docker/.env so the daemon and its clients receive matching values. Ports, volume paths, profiles, and health-check scheduling also remain root configuration inputs. See the Docker configuration guide. (#45359)

Source deployments

Use Python 3.13, Node.js 24.22.1 or later in the 24.x line, and pnpm 12.16.1. pnpm no longer provisions Node.js for the workspace, so install the required Node.js runtime separately. (#44976, #45094)

From the repository root:

uv sync --project api --frozen
uv run --directory api flask db upgrade
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. Refresh the standalone Agent Backend's locked server dependencies when deploying it separately.

difyctl

Install the matching 1.19.0 client and use difyctl help to discover the current server catalog. Refresh installed agent skills with difyctl install skills <dir>. Workflow and Chatflow automation should use the revised stop.run operation; message-based apps use stop.task.

Database migrations and existing data

Upgrading from 1.18.0 applies six migration revisions, ending at 53c10126d551. Apply the complete chain through the normal migration runner.

Operational changes to plan for include:

  • Storage-cleanup indexes (d7e9a1c3f502). Add reference indexes on message_files.upload_file_id, workflow_node_execution_offload.file_id, and workflow_draft_variable_files.upload_file_id. PostgreSQL creates them concurrently, but index construction still scans data and consumes I/O. Online upgrades reuse matching healthy indexes and reject conflicting or invalid definitions. Investigate an interrupted invalid build before retrying; do not drop healthy indexes as routine recovery. (#44982)
  • Tracing configuration uniqueness (53c10126d551). Keep one configuration per app/provider and add a unique index. When duplicates exist, the most recently updated row wins, with the ID breaking timestamp ties. Superseded rows are deleted; downgrading the index does not restore them. Retain a database backup. (#44673)
  • Extraction changes affect newly processed content. Re-import or re-index documents whose stored content was affected by the EPUB, EML, DOCX, CSV, Markdown, or Notion fixes. The repeated-PDF-preview fix prevents new duplicate assets for source uploads; it does not remove duplicates already stored. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434, #45053, #44684)
  • Tracing history is not rebuilt. Existing Agent trace-ledger data remains readable, but previously exported traces do not acquire the new nested spans. (#44673)

Detailed changes

New capabilities · tracing, packages, and Skills

Tracing and provider integrations

  • Consolidate delivery through the shared provider interface for Langfuse, LangSmith, Opik, Weave, Arize, Phoenix, Aliyun, MLflow, Databricks, and Tencent. Retryable exports resend the same trace unit with deterministic identifiers. (#44673)
  • Include called Workflow Tools' persisted execution frames in external exports, under their invoking Tool spans. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. (#44673)
  • Keep trace credentials write-only. Blank or omitted secrets preserve stored values; changing a destination host, endpoint, or URL requires entering its secrets again. (#44673)

Portable App packages

  • Package the workflows behind called Workflow Tools, including transitive dependencies, with a default maximum of 20 bundled tool workflows. Missing destination tools are recreated and published; existing tools are reused. Creating missing tools requires tool-management permission and sufficient app quota. Packages needing DSL-version confirmation are rejected in this flow, and apps created before an import failure are cleaned up. (#44592)
  • Always emit format v2 for App packages, including nested packages and packages without Workflow Tools. This does not change the separate roster-Agent package format. (#45353)
  • Workflow and API tool IDs no longer become spurious langgenius/<uuid> plugin dependencies during export. (#44592)

Skills and OpenAPI

  • Export drafts or published Skill versions, import folders, and publish through account-authenticated workspace operations. An import with a Skill ID replaces that Skill's draft; the imported SKILL.md name must match. Optional draft_hash checks reject stale replacements, but use second-resolution timestamps and do not detect edits made within the same second. (#44941)
  • Skill import drops operating-system junk, rejects unsafe or duplicate paths, enforces file/size limits, reuses identical binary assets, and removes assets written by a failed import. Literal dashes inside Skill frontmatter are preserved. (#44941, #43602)
  • The operation catalog publishes each operation's effect, and CLI help displays it. Workflow/Chatflow stopping uses stored run ownership and state; unknown runs return 404, and finished or otherwise non-stoppable runs return 409. Message-app stopping keeps its task-ID semantics. (#44587, #45314)
  • Add the experimental @dify/openapi-content-mapper package for typed API calls and query helpers inferred from OpenAPI sources, with reusable schema/input/output types and opt-in contract-compatible type subpaths. This is development groundwork; these changes do not migrate production Console or Marketplace calls away from their existing clients. (#44627, #44915)
Improvements · editing, accessibility, performance, and operations
  • Batch Agent file management: multi-select and multi-file drop, parallel uploads, one atomic binding request, retry using cached upload IDs, and protection against stale Composer saves overwriting newly bound files. Existing single-file endpoints remain compatible. (#44947)
  • More usable previews: highlighted text, on-demand PDF rendering, stable open previews, and explicit truncated-text notices across Agent files, Skills, and working directories. (#45032, #45045)
  • Direction and keyboard support: synchronized locale direction, broader right-to-left layouts, date/time pickers integrated with forms and focus containment, visible labels retained in accessible names, and consistent read-only controls. (#44621, #43869, #44638, #44650, #44593, #44755, #44772, #44589, #45036, #45375)
  • Safer editing dialogs: deletion, rename, metadata, annotation, member-role, and plugin-setting dialogs preserve their sessions and drafts, keep pending actions open, and restore focus after completion. Repeated deletion submissions are blocked while a request is pending. (#44618, #44623, #44643, #44646, #44698, #44736, #44743, #44810, #44825, #44788, #44715, #44652, #44838, #44830)
  • Clearer feedback: field errors and persistent notices appear near the controls they concern, with shared alert presentation across apps, workflows, knowledge, billing, and Skills. Cloud billing uses localized prompts for retryable and action-specific errors. (#45151, #45264, #45266, #45267, #45268, #45192)
  • Accurate Cloud quota displays: distinguish unlimited counts from zero-capacity App Run and trigger quotas, and interpret reset dates as Unix seconds. Pricing display data no longer doubles as live usage limits. (#45117, #45115)
  • Lower query overhead: segment pages load child chunks and attachments in batches; new reference indexes support app storage cleanup. (#45050, #44982)
  • Connection reuse: Gunicorn's configurable keep-alive defaults to 10 seconds, reducing failures caused by reusing connections after the server's shorter idle window. (#44839)
  • Docker configuration: service and provider overrides now reach the relevant containers, database commands, health checks, and WebSocket settings. The generator creates only a missing root .env, leaving optional overrides under operator control. (#45359, #45376)
Security enhancements
  • Workspace controls: enabling or disabling provider models requires an owner or administrator. Email-availability checks require account admission. (64fe95667b, 76979a1e24)
  • Request-scoped cookies: pooled SSRF clients retain response cookies only within the current outbound request and its redirects, preventing later requests from inheriting another request's cookies. (#44672)
  • Dataset token scope: resource access tokens can list only their explicitly bound active datasets; include_all=true cannot widen that scope. Legacy workspace Dataset API keys retain tenant-wide behavior without inheriting an injected owner's personal visibility filters. (#44840)
  • App access settings: importing DSL over an existing app preserves its Web App access mode, and converting an app inherits the source access mode. (#44700, #44857)
  • Tracing secrets and egress: configuration reads no longer return saved credentials, destination changes require secret re-entry, and provider traffic uses the shared outbound policy. (#44673)
  • Dependency hardening: update Authlib to 1.9.1, require LiteLLM 1.100.4 or later within its supported major version, move Agent Pydantic AI to 2.53.0 and Pillow to 13.0.0, update pypdf to 6.21.4, and refresh Werkzeug, GitPython, and other dependency fixes. The standalone Agent pins filelock 4.2.1; Docker build tooling updates uv to 0.13.4. These source updates do not claim to resolve every finding in external or Enterprise base images. (#44606, #44793, #44868, #44871, #44886, #45041, #45104, #45215, #45259, #45214, #45260)
Bug fixes · workflows, Agents, knowledge, APIs, and the web app

Workflows and execution

  • Restore structured-output fallback for models without native support and preserve JSON booleans instead of converting them to strings. (#44962)
  • Honor configured file and file-list defaults across Studio, published apps, and API execution. Explicit clearing stays distinct from omission, reset conversations restore defaults, and saving file defaults no longer sends browser Blob objects that cause 415 errors. (#44780, #45042)
  • Preserve numeric zero in required Studio inputs and previews, and preserve both zero and false in opening statements. Non-object file-reference payloads fall back to the original reference instead of failing unexpectedly. (#45005, #44833, #45088)
  • Admit streaming Workflow and Chatflow requests only once against app concurrency limits, so a limit of one accepts the single active request. Terminal Chatflow events now stop the execution watchdog and release its retained context. (#45038, #45029)
  • Preserve caller identity for scheduled Agent file access, use the UTC clock for the Start node's sys.timestamp, and order weekly schedule previews by date. Webhook query/form numbers retain integer precision and reject non-finite values. (#44796, #44847, #44718, #44706)
  • Refresh available workflow nodes when availability changes, retain generated variables when applying a generated prompt, escape variable-search highlighting, and preserve prompt-editor focus when variable metadata refreshes. (#44769, #45274, #44625, #44791)
  • Request clear-canvas confirmation only when clearing a previously nonempty saved draft, and wrap long workflow error messages. (#45028, #45106)

Agents, tools, and Skills

  • Persist refreshed OAuth credentials and serialize concurrent refreshes across tools and datasources, protecting rotating tokens and concurrent reauthorization. Temporary refresh failures return a temporary-unavailability response instead of incorrectly asking users to repair valid credentials. (#32195)
  • Reject late non-terminal events after an Agent stream has completed or been cancelled. Deduplicate plugin JSON output by content rather than formatting, and retain trailing partial action/thought prefixes in ReAct output. (#45080, #45297, #43353)
  • Stop serializing the entire prompt history into every Agent LLM gateway response chunk. Preserve request content, tool calls, multimodal content, usage, and quota settlement. (#45137)
  • Handle non-recording tracing parents and isolate concurrent Celery tracing contexts. (#44701, #44803, #45049)
  • Allow current Qwen flash models in Agent v2 and refresh suggested model patterns. Omit empty optional Agent variable inputs, and accept legacy comma-separated values for multiple-select tool parameters. (#44873, #44748, #45058)
  • Restore creator-based Agent edit permissions. Skill and snippet searches treat wildcard characters literally, and imported integration bundles retain their plugin icons. (#45040, #44922, #44708, #45112)

Knowledge and document processing

  • Remove index entries written by a document that was deleted during indexing. Partial QA-segment updates preserve an omitted answer and its contribution to counts. (#44364, #44997)
  • Include documents missing a metadata key in negative metadata filters, honor explicit top_k=0, normalize blank legacy retrieval settings on read, and use keyword retrieval for Economy datasets in retrieval previews. (#44753, #42980, #45020, #44895)
  • Restore Notion page listing and file import, keep failed page loads retryable, and surface Notion database HTTP failures. (#45053, #44893)
  • Read EPUB chapters in declared order without extracting archive members to disk; preserve already-decoded EML text; identify DOCX images by relationship type; support numeric CSV column labels; and keep headings inside Markdown code fences intact. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434)
  • Reuse extracted PDF image assets for repeated previews of the same source upload. Restore Service API file-document creation/update when tenant context is missing or the original dataset creator has left. (#44684, #44972)
  • Include users' own maintained datasets in their lists. (#44795)

APIs, files, and SDKs

  • Let MCP Chatflow generation commit its conversation session without a closed-transaction error. API-tool imports ignore non-method Swagger path keys. Suggested-question parsing retains brackets inside quoted questions, and missing citation resources return an empty list. (#44636, #44992, #44916, #43036)
  • Normalize remote Content-Type values, preserve detected media types for uploads accepted through “Other File Types,” and apply media-specific limits during remote-upload preflight. (#44677, #41292, #44273)
  • Report download HTTP failures instead of passing error pages to the plugin installer. Distinguish Squid-generated denial responses from upstream authentication errors, preserve GitHub import paths containing blob, and reject incompatible multipart file shapes consistently. (#44333, #44841, #44280, #44903)
  • The Node.js SDK accepts long knowledge-document text, handles CR/LF/CRLF SSE framing and a leading BOM, and accepts an empty pagination cursor as the first page. (#44679, #44263, #44265)
  • The PHP SDK serializes empty app inputs as JSON objects, avoids buffering streaming Workflow and text-to-audio responses, and sends last_id for conversation pagination while preserving its public method signature. (#44675, #44271, #44659)

Web app and workspace

  • Keep newly created, user-maintained apps visible in Studio and preserve primary navigation across Console routes. Calculate log-period boundaries from the current date. (#44929, #44633, #45360)
  • Use navigable links in document menus, open publisher destinations in new tabs, and advance integration-tour steps without reloading the page. (#44694, #44808, #44934, #44944)
  • Respect Marketplace availability across template and plugin entry points and render emoji-ID icons in recommended cards. (#45009, #45027, #45066)
  • Preserve annotation editor drafts and voice-input focus, and add the Simplified Chinese account-deletion success email template. (#44810, #44825, #45169, #43504)
Environment variables and integration changes
Setting Change in 1.19.0
OPS_TRACE_QUEUE New; defaults to ops_trace_v2. Shared by trace delivery/retries, Agent trace work, payload cleanup, and sandbox metering. API, workers, and Beat must agree.
OPS_TRACE_EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS New; defaults to 6 total attempts for retryable trace exports.
ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOAD_SWEEP_TASK New; defaults to true, enabling daily cleanup of orphaned new-pipeline trace payloads.
APP_PACKAGE_MAX_WORKFLOW_TOOLS New; defaults to 20 bundled Workflow Tool workflows per App package.
GUNICORN_KEEP_ALIVE New entrypoint setting; defaults to 10 seconds.

The old OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS, and OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS settings are removed. Existing Agent application-tracing opt-in settings remain supported. (#44673)

For Docker, use envs/core-services/api-worker.defaults as the reference for common API/worker/Beat settings and api-worker.env for new overrides. Existing shared.env remains compatible. Tracked defaults load automatically; root .env and explicit service overrides still take precedence. Review the service-specific references rather than replacing local files with fresh templates. (#45359, #45376)

Endpoint compatibility

  • Replace deprecated Console profile-update POST calls to /account/name, /account/avatar, /account/interface-language, /account/interface-theme, and /account/timezone with PATCH /console/api/account/profile. Avatar URL reads remain available. (#45015)
  • Custom clients of GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/trace-config must consume configured_secrets instead of expecting saved secret values. (#44673)
  • For Workflow and Chatflow OpenAPI calls, use POST /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}:stop (stop.run) and GET /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}/events (get.run.event). Chat, Agent Chat, and Completion retain the task-ID stop route under stop.task. (#44587)
  • Cloud education verification returns an explicit status: eligible | not_eligible result; only eligible results contain a token. The corresponding internal billing service must support this response contract. (#45165)

Full Changelog: 1.18.0 to the 1.19.0

Configure shared plugin credentials, PLUGIN_DAEMON_KEY and PLUGIN_DIFY_INNER_API_KEY, in root docker/.env so the daemon and its clients receive matching values. Ports, volume paths, profiles, and health-check scheduling also remain root configuration inputs. See the Docker configuration guide. (#45359)

Source deployments

Use Python 3.13, Node.js 24.22.1 or later in the 24.x line, and pnpm 12.16.1. pnpm no longer provisions Node.js for the workspace, so install the required Node.js runtime separately. (#44976, #45094)

From the repository root:

uv sync --project api --frozen
uv run --directory api flask db upgrade
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. Refresh the standalone Agent Backend's locked server dependencies when deploying it separately.

difyctl

Install the matching 1.19.0 client and use difyctl help to discover the current server catalog. Refresh installed agent skills with difyctl install skills <dir>. Workflow and Chatflow automation should use the revised stop.run operation; message-based apps use stop.task.

Database migrations and existing data

Upgrading from 1.18.0 applies six migration revisions, ending at 53c10126d551. Apply the complete chain through the normal migration runner.

Operational changes to plan for include:

  • Storage-cleanup indexes (d7e9a1c3f502). Add reference indexes on message_files.upload_file_id, workflow_node_execution_offload.file_id, and workflow_draft_variable_files.upload_file_id. PostgreSQL creates them concurrently, but index construction still scans data and consumes I/O. Online upgrades reuse matching healthy indexes and reject conflicting or invalid definitions. Investigate an interrupted invalid build before retrying; do not drop healthy indexes as routine recovery. (#44982)
  • Tracing configuration uniqueness (53c10126d551). Keep one configuration per app/provider and add a unique index. When duplicates exist, the most recently updated row wins, with the ID breaking timestamp ties. Superseded rows are deleted; downgrading the index does not restore them. Retain a database backup. (#44673)
  • Extraction changes affect newly processed content. Re-import or re-index documents whose stored content was affected by the EPUB, EML, DOCX, CSV, Markdown, or Notion fixes. The repeated-PDF-preview fix prevents new duplicate assets for source uploads; it does not remove duplicates already stored. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434, #45053, #44684)
  • Tracing history is not rebuilt. Existing Agent trace-ledger data remains readable, but previously exported traces do not acquire the new nested spans. (#44673)

Detailed changes

New capabilities · tracing, packages, and Skills

Tracing and provider integrations

  • Consolidate delivery through the shared provider interface for Langfuse, LangSmith, Opik, Weave, Arize, Phoenix, Aliyun, MLflow, Databricks, and Tencent. Retryable exports resend the same trace unit with deterministic identifiers. (#44673)
  • Include called Workflow Tools' persisted execution frames in external exports, under their invoking Tool spans. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. (#44673)
  • Keep trace credentials write-only. Blank or omitted secrets preserve stored values; changing a destination host, endpoint, or URL requires entering its secrets again. (#44673)

Portable App packages

  • Package the workflows behind called Workflow Tools, including transitive dependencies, with a default maximum of 20 bundled tool workflows. Missing destination tools are recreated and published; existing tools are reused. Creating missing tools requires tool-management permission and sufficient app quota. Packages needing DSL-version confirmation are rejected in this flow, and apps created before an import failure are cleaned up. (#44592)
  • Always emit format v2 for App packages, including nested packages and packages without Workflow Tools. This does not change the separate roster-Agent package format. (#45353)
  • Workflow and API tool IDs no longer become spurious langgenius/<uuid> plugin dependencies during export. (#44592)

Skills and OpenAPI

  • Export drafts or published Skill versions, import folders, and publish through account-authenticated workspace operations. An import with a Skill ID replaces that Skill's draft; the imported SKILL.md name must match. Optional draft_hash checks reject stale replacements, but use second-resolution timestamps and do not detect edits made within the same second. (#44941)
  • Skill import drops operating-system junk, rejects unsafe or duplicate paths, enforces file/size limits, reuses identical binary assets, and removes assets written by a failed import. Literal dashes inside Skill frontmatter are preserved. (#44941, #43602)
  • The operation catalog publishes each operation's effect, and CLI help displays it. Workflow/Chatflow stopping uses stored run ownership and state; unknown runs return 404, and finished or otherwise non-stoppable runs return 409. Message-app stopping keeps its task-ID semantics. (#44587, #45314)
  • Add the experimental @dify/openapi-content-mapper package for typed API calls and query helpers inferred from OpenAPI sources, with reusable schema/input/output types and opt-in contract-compatible type subpaths. This is development groundwork; these changes do not migrate production Console or Marketplace calls away from their existing clients. (#44627, #44915)
Improvements · editing, accessibility, performance, and operations
  • Batch Agent file management: multi-select and multi-file drop, parallel uploads, one atomic binding request, retry using cached upload IDs, and protection against stale Composer saves overwriting newly bound files. Existing single-file endpoints remain compatible. (#44947)
  • More usable previews: highlighted text, on-demand PDF rendering, stable open previews, and explicit truncated-text notices across Agent files, Skills, and working directories. (#45032, #45045)
  • Direction and keyboard support: synchronized locale direction, broader right-to-left layouts, date/time pickers integrated with forms and focus containment, visible labels retained in accessible names, and consistent read-only controls. (#44621, #43869, #44638, #44650, #44593, #44755, #44772, #44589, #45036, #45375)
  • Safer editing dialogs: deletion, rename, metadata, annotation, member-role, and plugin-setting dialogs preserve their sessions and drafts, keep pending actions open, and restore focus after completion. Repeated deletion submissions are blocked while a request is pending. (#44618, #44623, #44643, #44646, #44698, #44736, #44743, #44810, #44825, #44788, #44715, #44652, #44838, #44830)
  • Clearer feedback: field errors and persistent notices appear near the controls they concern, with shared alert presentation across apps, workflows, knowledge, billing, and Skills. Cloud billing uses localized prompts for retryable and action-specific errors. (#45151, #45264, #45266, #45267, #45268, #45192)
  • Accurate Cloud quota displays: distinguish unlimited counts from zero-capacity App Run and trigger quotas, and interpret reset dates as Unix seconds. Pricing display data no longer doubles as live usage limits. (#45117, #45115)
  • Lower query overhead: segment pages load child chunks and attachments in batches; new reference indexes support app storage cleanup. (#45050, #44982)
  • Connection reuse: Gunicorn's configurable keep-alive defaults to 10 seconds, reducing failures caused by reusing connections after the server's shorter idle window. (#44839)
  • Docker configuration: service and provider overrides now reach the relevant containers, database commands, health checks, and WebSocket settings. The generator creates only a missing root .env, leaving optional overrides under operator control. (#45359, #45376)
Security enhancements
  • Workspace controls: enabling or disabling provider models requires an owner or administrator. Email-availability checks require account admission. (64fe95667b, 76979a1e24)
  • Request-scoped cookies: pooled SSRF clients retain response cookies only within the current outbound request and its redirects, preventing later requests from inheriting another request's cookies. (#44672)
  • Dataset token scope: resource access tokens can list only their explicitly bound active datasets; include_all=true cannot widen that scope. Legacy workspace Dataset API keys retain tenant-wide behavior without inheriting an injected owner's personal visibility filters. (#44840)
  • App access settings: importing DSL over an existing app preserves its Web App access mode, and converting an app inherits the source access mode. (#44700, #44857)
  • Tracing secrets and egress: configuration reads no longer return saved credentials, destination changes require secret re-entry, and provider traffic uses the shared outbound policy. (#44673)
  • Dependency hardening: update Authlib to 1.9.1, require LiteLLM 1.100.4 or later within its supported major version, move Agent Pydantic AI to 2.53.0 and Pillow to 13.0.0, update pypdf to 6.21.4, and refresh Werkzeug, GitPython, and other dependency fixes. The standalone Agent pins filelock 4.2.1; Docker build tooling updates uv to 0.13.4. These source updates do not claim to resolve every finding in external or Enterprise base images. (#44606, #44793, #44868, #44871, #44886, #45041, #45104, #45215, #45259, #45214, #45260)
Bug fixes · workflows, Agents, knowledge, APIs, and the web app

Workflows and execution

  • Restore structured-output fallback for models without native support and preserve JSON booleans instead of converting them to strings. (#44962)
  • Honor configured file and file-list defaults across Studio, published apps, and API execution. Explicit clearing stays distinct from omission, reset conversations restore defaults, and saving file defaults no longer sends browser Blob objects that cause 415 errors. (#44780, #45042)
  • Preserve numeric zero in required Studio inputs and previews, and preserve both zero and false in opening statements. Non-object file-reference payloads fall back to the original reference instead of failing unexpectedly. (#45005, #44833, #45088)
  • Admit streaming Workflow and Chatflow requests only once against app concurrency limits, so a limit of one accepts the single active request. Terminal Chatflow events now stop the execution watchdog and release its retained context. (#45038, #45029)
  • Preserve caller identity for scheduled Agent file access, use the UTC clock for the Start node's sys.timestamp, and order weekly schedule previews by date. Webhook query/form numbers retain integer precision and reject non-finite values. (#44796, #44847, #44718, #44706)
  • Refresh available workflow nodes when availability changes, retain generated variables when applying a generated prompt, escape variable-search highlighting, and preserve prompt-editor focus when variable metadata refreshes. (#44769, #45274, #44625, #44791)
  • Request clear-canvas confirmation only when clearing a previously nonempty saved draft, and wrap long workflow error messages. (#45028, #45106)

Agents, tools, and Skills

  • Persist refreshed OAuth credentials and serialize concurrent refreshes across tools and datasources, protecting rotating tokens and concurrent reauthorization. Temporary refresh failures return a temporary-unavailability response instead of incorrectly asking users to repair valid credentials. (#32195)
  • Reject late non-terminal events after an Agent stream has completed or been cancelled. Deduplicate plugin JSON output by content rather than formatting, and retain trailing partial action/thought prefixes in ReAct output. (#45080, #45297, #43353)
  • Stop serializing the entire prompt history into every Agent LLM gateway response chunk. Preserve request content, tool calls, multimodal content, usage, and quota settlement. (#45137)
  • Handle non-recording tracing parents and isolate concurrent Celery tracing contexts. (#44701, #44803, #45049)
  • Allow current Qwen flash models in Agent v2 and refresh suggested model patterns. Omit empty optional Agent variable inputs, and accept legacy comma-separated values for multiple-select tool parameters. (#44873, #44748, #45058)
  • Restore creator-based Agent edit permissions. Skill and snippet searches treat wildcard characters literally, and imported integration bundles retain their plugin icons. (#45040, #44922, #44708, #45112)

Knowledge and document processing

  • Remove index entries written by a document that was deleted during indexing. Partial QA-segment updates preserve an omitted answer and its contribution to counts. (#44364, #44997)
  • Include documents missing a metadata key in negative metadata filters, honor explicit top_k=0, normalize blank legacy retrieval settings on read, and use keyword retrieval for Economy datasets in retrieval previews. (#44753, #42980, #45020, #44895)
  • Restore Notion page listing and file import, keep failed page loads retryable, and surface Notion database HTTP failures. (#45053, #44893)
  • Read EPUB chapters in declared order without extracting archive members to disk; preserve already-decoded EML text; identify DOCX images by relationship type; support numeric CSV column labels; and keep headings inside Markdown code fences intact. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434)
  • Reuse extracted PDF image assets for repeated previews of the same source upload. Restore Service API file-document creation/update when tenant context is missing or the original dataset creator has left. (#44684, #44972)
  • Include users' own maintained datasets in their lists. (#44795)

APIs, files, and SDKs

  • Let MCP Chatflow generation commit its conversation session without a closed-transaction error. API-tool imports ignore non-method Swagger path keys. Suggested-question parsing retains brackets inside quoted questions, and missing citation resources return an empty list. (#44636, #44992, #44916, #43036)
  • Normalize remote Content-Type values, preserve detected media types for uploads accepted through “Other File Types,” and apply media-specific limits during remote-upload preflight. (#44677, #41292, #44273)
  • Report download HTTP failures instead of passing error pages to the plugin installer. Distinguish Squid-generated denial responses from upstream authentication errors, preserve GitHub import paths containing blob, and reject incompatible multipart file shapes consistently. (#44333, #44841, #44280, #44903)
  • The Node.js SDK accepts long knowledge-document text, handles CR/LF/CRLF SSE framing and a leading BOM, and accepts an empty pagination cursor as the first page. (#44679, #44263, #44265)
  • The PHP SDK serializes empty app inputs as JSON objects, avoids buffering streaming Workflow and text-to-audio responses, and sends last_id for conversation pagination while preserving its public method signature. (#44675, #44271, #44659)

Web app and workspace

  • Keep newly created, user-maintained apps visible in Studio and preserve primary navigation across Console routes. Calculate log-period boundaries from the current date. (#44929, #44633, #45360)
  • Use navigable links in document menus, open publisher destinations in new tabs, and advance integration-tour steps without reloading the page. (#44694, #44808, #44934, #44944)
  • Respect Marketplace availability across template and plugin entry points and render emoji-ID icons in recommended cards. (#45009, #45027, #45066)
  • Preserve annotation editor drafts and voice-input focus, and add the Simplified Chinese account-deletion success email template. (#44810, #44825, #45169, #43504)
Environment variables and integration changes
Setting Change in 1.19.0
OPS_TRACE_QUEUE New; defaults to ops_trace_v2. Shared by trace delivery/retries, Agent trace work, payload cleanup, and sandbox metering. API, workers, and Beat must agree.
OPS_TRACE_EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS New; defaults to 6 total attempts for retryable trace exports.
ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOAD_SWEEP_TASK New; defaults to true, enabling daily cleanup of orphaned new-pipeline trace payloads.
APP_PACKAGE_MAX_WORKFLOW_TOOLS New; defaults to 20 bundled Workflow Tool workflows per App package.
GUNICORN_KEEP_ALIVE New entrypoint setting; defaults to 10 seconds.

The old OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS, and OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS settings are removed. Existing Agent application-tracing opt-in settings remain supported. (#44673)

For Docker, use envs/core-services/api-worker.defaults as the reference for common API/worker/Beat settings and api-worker.env for new overrides. Existing shared.env remains compatible. Tracked defaults load automatically; root .env and explicit service overrides still take precedence. Review the service-specific references rather than replacing local files with fresh templates. (#45359, #45376)

Endpoint compatibility

  • Replace deprecated Console profile-update POST calls to /account/name, /account/avatar, /account/interface-language, /account/interface-theme, and /account/timezone with PATCH /console/api/account/profile. Avatar URL reads remain available. (#45015)
  • Custom clients of GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/trace-config must consume configured_secrets instead of expecting saved secret values. (#44673)
  • For Workflow and Chatflow OpenAPI calls, use POST /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}:stop (stop.run) and GET /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}/events (get.run.event). Chat, Agent Chat, and Completion retain the task-ID stop route under stop.task. (#44587)
  • Cloud education verification returns an explicit status: eligible | not_eligible result; only eligible results contain a token. The corresponding internal billing service must support this response contract. (#45165)

Full Changelog: 1.18.0 to the 1.19.0

Dify 1.19.0 brings nested workflow tracing to your observability tools. Follow a workflow into the Workflow Tools it calls, inspect the steps inside each invocation, and keep the LLM context alongside the execution tree.

This release also makes Workflow Tools portable with App packages, adds Skill Hub automation, and makes Agent files easier to upload and preview. The bundled plugin daemon is upgraded to 0.6.14-local.

Release highlights · Upgrade guide · Detailed changes

Release highlights

Nested workflow tracing

See what happens inside a Workflow Tool, all the way down to its LLM calls.

Building on the Console drilldown introduced in 1.18.0, new external traces now include the persisted execution steps inside called Workflow Tools. Child steps appear beneath the Tool span that invoked them, preserving the hierarchy across nested and repeated calls. (#44673)

From the outer workflow to a nested LLM call: the execution tree and formatted messages, together in Langfuse. Screenshot from #44673.

  • Follow the hierarchy. Expand called Workflow Tools to see their internal execution steps under the invoking Tool span.
  • Understand each invocation. Repeated calls and failures retain their place in the trace.
  • Keep the LLM context. Inspect formatted prompts and responses, token usage, and project, trace, and observation links.

Note

Your saved provider settings continue to work. The richer hierarchy applies to new executions; historical traces are not backfilled. Independently nested workflow runs remain separate traces linked by parent identifiers. For rolling deployments, follow the tracing queue transition below.

Take Workflow Tools with your apps

Export an app and bring the workflows behind its Workflow Tools with it. .ifpkg packages include those workflows at their bound versions, including transitive dependencies. Import reuses tools already in the destination workspace and recreates, publishes, and registers missing ones, remapping their references. (#44592)

All Dify app exports now use package format v2, including apps without Workflow Tools. Existing v1 imports and explicit YAML export remain supported. See the upgrade guide before importing new packages into older installations. (#45353)

Upload together. Preview in place.

Select or drop multiple Agent configuration files and upload them in parallel. Successful uploads are bound in one atomic batch, concurrent Composer saves preserve the latest files, and Prompt uploads keep the cursor position while inserting multiple references. (#44947)

Read PDFs inline, inspect source files with syntax highlighting, and see when text has been truncated. Previews cover configured files, Skill members, and working-directory files, with a download action when a PDF cannot be loaded. (#45032, #45045)

See Agent file uploads and previews

Read a PDF directly in the Agent file preview and switch between project files.

Select several files and upload them together.

Inspect source files with syntax highlighting and line numbers.

Developer spotlight

Manage workspace Skills through OpenAPI and difyctl. Find and inspect Skills, export a draft or published version, import local files, and publish a new version from the command line. (#44941)

The six Skill commands
Command Capability
difyctl get skill List Skills, with keyword and tag filters.
difyctl describe skill Read details, the draft hash, and latest published version.
difyctl get skill version List published versions.
difyctl export skill Export the draft or a selected published version as ZIP.
difyctl import skill --files <dir> Create a Skill or replace an existing Skill's draft from local files.
difyctl publish skill Publish the draft as a new version.

These operations require an account caller, the corresponding workspace permissions, and Skills to be enabled. Import does not publish. Importing over an existing Skill is classified as destructive; the operation catalog and CLI help distinguish read, write, and destructive operations. (#44941, #45314, #44587)

Upgrade guide

Important

Read the upgrade guide before deploying. Docker Compose now requires v2.35.0 or later. Preserve existing environment files, upgrade the Dify components together, and use the new tracing queue during rolling deployments. New App packages use format v2 and require a compatible destination importer. The bundled plugin daemon moves to 0.6.14-local.

Compatibility and rollout

  1. Back up first. Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, deployment secrets, and environment files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade.
  2. Upgrade the components together. Use matching 1.19.0 API, worker, web, Agent Backend, and Local sandbox images, with plugin daemon 0.6.14-local. Keep the existing Local sandbox authentication token and any configured PASSWORD_PEPPER unchanged. If upgrading from before 1.18.0, also follow the 1.18.0 upgrade guide.
  3. Use Docker Compose 2.35.0 or later. This is the minimum supported version for root .env overrides to take precedence when Compose resolves service defaults. Check your installed version with docker compose version. (#45359)
  4. Keep tracked defaults separate from local overrides. Bundled docker/envs/**/*.defaults files load automatically. Customize a service through its matching local .env file, using the override path documented in the defaults file; root docker/.env holds deployment inputs and explicit overrides. Preserve existing .env files and edit them in place. Review accidentally empty assignments and values pinned by older template copies before upgrading. (#45359, #45376)
  5. Existing shared.env files remain supported. Common API, worker, and Beat customizations now belong in docker/envs/core-services/api-worker.env. Compose still reads legacy docker/envs/core-services/shared.env first, then api-worker.env, so api-worker.env wins when both set conflicting values. Root docker/.env takes precedence over both. An unchanged copy of api-worker.defaults preserves existing shared.env customizations. See the Docker configuration guide. (#45376)
  6. Separate tracing queues during a rolling upgrade. New tasks default to OPS_TRACE_QUEUE=ops_trace_v2; API, workers, and Beat must agree. Custom CELERY_QUEUES, CELERY_WORKER_QUEUES, or --queues lists must include the new queue. Keep old tracing workers on ops_trace until old producers and all their queued, active, reserved, scheduled, and retry work have finished. Do not purge the old queue or ask the new retired handler to export legacy messages. See the tracing rollout guide. (#44673)
  7. Upgrade package destinations before importing new App packages. New app packages always use format v2. Older importers, including builds with the earlier strict v2 rule, may reject them. Version 1 imports remain supported on 1.19.0. Explicit YAML export remains available, but does not carry bundled Workflow Tool dependencies. (#44592, #45353)

Once the 1.19.0 release tag and images are published, stop a single-stack deployment gracefully, switch to the release, retain and review configuration, then pull and start the new images:

cd dify/docker
docker compose stop -t -1
git fetch --tags
git checkout 1.19.0
# Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here.
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

  • Docker configuration: service and provider overrides now reach the relevant containers, database commands, health checks, and WebSocket settings. The generator creates only a missing root .env, leaving optional overrides under operator control. (#45359, #45376)
Security enhancements
  • Workspace controls: enabling or disabling provider models requires an owner or administrator. Email-availability checks require account admission. (64fe95667b, 76979a1e24)
  • Request-scoped cookies: pooled SSRF clients retain response cookies only within the current outbound request and its redirects, preventing later requests from inheriting another request's cookies. (#44672)
  • Dataset token scope: resource access tokens can list only their explicitly bound active datasets; include_all=true cannot widen that scope. Legacy workspace Dataset API keys retain tenant-wide behavior without inheriting an injected owner's personal visibility filters. (#44840)
  • App access settings: importing DSL over an existing app preserves its Web App access mode, and converting an app inherits the source access mode. (#44700, #44857)
  • Tracing secrets and egress: configuration reads no longer return saved credentials, destination changes require secret re-entry, and provider traffic uses the shared outbound policy. (#44673)
  • Dependency hardening: update Authlib to 1.9.1, require LiteLLM 1.100.4 or later within its supported major version, move Agent Pydantic AI to 2.53.0 and Pillow to 13.0.0, update pypdf to 6.21.4, and refresh Werkzeug, GitPython, and other dependency fixes. The standalone Agent pins filelock 4.2.1; Docker build tooling updates uv to 0.13.4. These source updates do not claim to resolve every finding in external or Enterprise base images. (#44606, #44793, #44868, #44871, #44886, #45041, #45104, #45215, #45259, #45214, #45260)
Bug fixes · workflows, Agents, knowledge, APIs, and the web app

Workflows and execution

  • Restore structured-output fallback for models without native support and preserve JSON booleans instead of converting them to strings. (#44962)
  • Honor configured file and file-list defaults across Studio, published apps, and API execution. Explicit clearing stays distinct from omission, reset conversations restore defaults, and saving file defaults no longer sends browser Blob objects that cause 415 errors. (#44780, #45042)
  • Preserve numeric zero in required Studio inputs and previews, and preserve both zero and false in opening statements. Non-object file-reference payloads fall back to the original reference instead of failing unexpectedly. (#45005, #44833, #45088)
  • Admit streaming Workflow and Chatflow requests only once against app concurrency limits, so a limit of one accepts the single active request. Terminal Chatflow events now stop the execution watchdog and release its retained context. (#45038, #45029)
  • Preserve caller identity for scheduled Agent file access, use the UTC clock for the Start node's sys.timestamp, and order weekly schedule previews by date. Webhook query/form numbers retain integer precision and reject non-finite values. (#44796, #44847, #44718, #44706)
  • Refresh available workflow nodes when availability changes, retain generated variables when applying a generated prompt, escape variable-search highlighting, and preserve prompt-editor focus when variable metadata refreshes. (#44769, #45274, #44625, #44791)
  • Request clear-canvas confirmation only when clearing a previously nonempty saved draft, and wrap long workflow error messages. (#45028, #45106)

Agents, tools, and Skills

  • Persist refreshed OAuth credentials and serialize concurrent refreshes across tools and datasources, protecting rotating tokens and concurrent reauthorization. Temporary refresh failures return a temporary-unavailability response instead of incorrectly asking users to repair valid credentials. (#32195)
  • Reject late non-terminal events after an Agent stream has completed or been cancelled. Deduplicate plugin JSON output by content rather than formatting, and retain trailing partial action/thought prefixes in ReAct output. (#45080, #45297, #43353)
  • Stop serializing the entire prompt history into every Agent LLM gateway response chunk. Preserve request content, tool calls, multimodal content, usage, and quota settlement. (#45137)
  • Handle non-recording tracing parents and isolate concurrent Celery tracing contexts. (#44701, #44803, #45049)
  • Allow current Qwen flash models in Agent v2 and refresh suggested model patterns. Omit empty optional Agent variable inputs, and accept legacy comma-separated values for multiple-select tool parameters. (#44873, #44748, #45058)
  • Restore creator-based Agent edit permissions. Skill and snippet searches treat wildcard characters literally, and imported integration bundles retain their plugin icons. (#45040, #44922, #44708, #45112)

Knowledge and document processing

  • Remove index entries written by a document that was deleted during indexing. Partial QA-segment updates preserve an omitted answer and its contribution to counts. (#44364, #44997)
  • Include documents missing a metadata key in negative metadata filters, honor explicit top_k=0, normalize blank legacy retrieval settings on read, and use keyword retrieval for Economy datasets in retrieval previews. (#44753, #42980, #45020, #44895)
  • Restore Notion page listing and file import, keep failed page loads retryable, and surface Notion database HTTP failures. (#45053, #44893)
  • Read EPUB chapters in declared order without extracting archive members to disk; preserve already-decoded EML text; identify DOCX images by relationship type; support numeric CSV column labels; and keep headings inside Markdown code fences intact. (#44836, #44953, #44905, #43505, #43434)
  • Reuse extracted PDF image assets for repeated previews of the same source upload. Restore Service API file-document creation/update when tenant context is missing or the original dataset creator has left. (#44684, #44972)
  • Include users' own maintained datasets in their lists. (#44795)

APIs, files, and SDKs

  • Let MCP Chatflow generation commit its conversation session without a closed-transaction error. API-tool imports ignore non-method Swagger path keys. Suggested-question parsing retains brackets inside quoted questions, and missing citation resources return an empty list. (#44636, #44992, #44916, #43036)
  • Normalize remote Content-Type values, preserve detected media types for uploads accepted through “Other File Types,” and apply media-specific limits during remote-upload preflight. (#44677, #41292, #44273)
  • Report download HTTP failures instead of passing error pages to the plugin installer. Distinguish Squid-generated denial responses from upstream authentication errors, preserve GitHub import paths containing blob, and reject incompatible multipart file shapes consistently. (#44333, #44841, #44280, #44903)
  • The Node.js SDK accepts long knowledge-document text, handles CR/LF/CRLF SSE framing and a leading BOM, and accepts an empty pagination cursor as the first page. (#44679, #44263, #44265)
  • The PHP SDK serializes empty app inputs as JSON objects, avoids buffering streaming Workflow and text-to-audio responses, and sends last_id for conversation pagination while preserving its public method signature. (#44675, #44271, #44659)

Web app and workspace

  • Keep newly created, user-maintained apps visible in Studio and preserve primary navigation across Console routes. Calculate log-period boundaries from the current date. (#44929, #44633, #45360)
  • Use navigable links in document menus, open publisher destinations in new tabs, and advance integration-tour steps without reloading the page. (#44694, #44808, #44934, #44944)
  • Respect Marketplace availability across template and plugin entry points and render emoji-ID icons in recommended cards. (#45009, #45027, #45066)
  • Preserve annotation editor drafts and voice-input focus, and add the Simplified Chinese account-deletion success email template. (#44810, #44825, #45169, #43504)
Environment variables and integration changes
Setting Change in 1.19.0
OPS_TRACE_QUEUE New; defaults to ops_trace_v2. Shared by trace delivery/retries, Agent trace work, payload cleanup, and sandbox metering. API, workers, and Beat must agree.
OPS_TRACE_EXPORT_MAX_ATTEMPTS New; defaults to 6 total attempts for retryable trace exports.
ENABLE_TRACE_PAYLOAD_SWEEP_TASK New; defaults to true, enabling daily cleanup of orphaned new-pipeline trace payloads.
APP_PACKAGE_MAX_WORKFLOW_TOOLS New; defaults to 20 bundled Workflow Tool workflows per App package.
GUNICORN_KEEP_ALIVE New entrypoint setting; defaults to 10 seconds.

The old OPS_TRACE_UNIFIED_ENABLED, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_MAX_RETRIES, OPS_TRACE_RETRYABLE_DISPATCH_DELAY_SECONDS, and OPS_TRACE_PARENT_CONTEXT_TTL_SECONDS settings are removed. Existing Agent application-tracing opt-in settings remain supported. (#44673)

For Docker, use envs/core-services/api-worker.defaults as the reference for common API/worker/Beat settings and api-worker.env for new overrides. Existing shared.env remains compatible. Tracked defaults load automatically; root .env and explicit service overrides still take precedence. Review the service-specific references rather than replacing local files with fresh templates. (#45359, #45376)

Endpoint compatibility

  • Replace deprecated Console profile-update POST calls to /account/name, /account/avatar, /account/interface-language, /account/interface-theme, and /account/timezone with PATCH /console/api/account/profile. Avatar URL reads remain available. (#45015)
  • Custom clients of GET /console/api/apps/{app_id}/trace-config must consume configured_secrets instead of expecting saved secret values. (#44673)
  • For Workflow and Chatflow OpenAPI calls, use POST /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}:stop (stop.run) and GET /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}/runs/{run_id}/events (get.run.event). Chat, Agent Chat, and Completion retain the task-ID stop route under stop.task. (#44587)
  • Cloud education verification returns an explicit status: eligible | not_eligible result; only eligible results contain a token. The corresponding internal billing service must support this response contract. (#45165)

Full Changelog: 1.18.0 to the 1.19.0

item.itunes:summary:
Dify 1.18.0 brings Agents that route workflows, portable app packages, deeper visibility into nested workflow runs, and the opt-in Agent Knowledge Base experience. OpenAPI and the new difyctl expand how you build and manage apps from the command line.

Important

Read the upgrade guide below before deploying. Upgrade the API, workers, Agent Backend, and Agent runtime images together. Local Agent sandboxes require a non-empty authentication token, and Agent Backend uses a new run protocol. Source installations require Python 3.13. Install the new difyctl client and sign in again. Preserve your existing PASSWORD_PEPPER configuration.

Release highlights

Agents that choose the next step

Let an Agent decide which workflow branch to take. Enable Output Routes, give each route a selection condition, and connect it to the next step—such as resolving a request directly or handing it to a specialist. The read-only switch output exposes the chosen route. (#42599)

Output Routes configuration with two branches in the workflow editor.

Plain Agent v2 nodes also stream text as it is generated. Structured results, routed results, and nodes using default-value error handling remain buffered. (#43986)

Portable apps in one package

Move an app with its supported resources in a single .ifpkg package. Workflow and Chatflow packages carry inline Agents, Skills, and their files; imports recreate those resources in the destination workspace and remap references. File and URL imports support both packages and YAML, and explicit YAML export remains available. (#42066, #42579, #42626, #42863)

Studio's .ifpkg import preview.

See inside nested workflow runs

Open a Workflow Tool invocation from the run history and inspect the child workflow's individual steps. Nested tools now run as child graphs with coordinated pause, resume, stop, and file outputs. Access checks protect the source app's details. (#40277, #42819, #42820, #42821, #42822)

Trace drilldown into a successful Workflow Tool invocation.

Nested usage and step totals can still be approximate, particularly after a pause or stop. Console drilldown and external trace export have different scopes; see the full feature details below.

Agent Knowledge Base · Beta

Create a knowledge space for your agents, add files or connect sources, and inspect document processing, metadata, retrieval traces, and quality evaluations in one place. The new Knowledge Retrieval node and Agent integrations share access-controlled KnowledgeFS spaces. Classic Knowledge remains available. This is an opt-in integration with a separate service and database; see the deployment requirements below. (#44165)

Will soon be available on cloud.dify.ai

Developer spotlight

Build and manage apps with OpenAPI and difyctl. The CLI discovers commands from the server's operation catalog, with searchable help and support for Workflow and Chatflow creation, DSL import/export, settings, environment variables, publishing, and version restoration. Draft hashes protect concurrent edits. (#42487, #42608, #43067)

Install the bundled skill for agents building Dify apps:

difyctl install skills <dir>

The new client requires a fresh sign-in; see the deployment instructions below. (#43819)

Upgrade guide

Compatibility and Rollout

  1. Back up first. Retain the database, vector-store data, uploaded files, Agent snapshot/workspace storage, and all deployment secrets and env files. Use a maintenance window for a single-stack upgrade.
  2. Upgrade the Agent components together. /runs now accepts composition v2 and rejects v1 requests. Existing session snapshots are converted on read and saved as v2; old runtimes cannot read newly saved v2 snapshots. Direct Agent Backend integrations must update their request format. The old Agent-specific AskHuman tool and deferred resume path are removed: historical Agent forms no longer resume execution, while shared Workflow Human Input nodes remain supported. (#43833)
  3. Retire old workflow consumers before admitting new-version traffic. Let in-flight runs finish, then replace legacy workers/resume consumers so they cannot process the shared queue without the new cancellation guards. Legacy paused task IDs can be recovered from valid saved invocation snapshots within the existing access scope; missing or invalid snapshots require separate recovery. Nested usage totals retain the limitation noted above. (#40277)
  4. Configure the Local sandbox token before restart. Supply a high-entropy secret through the shared Compose interpolation source. The 1.17.1 runtime image does not support the new --require-auth-token flag; deploy the matching 1.18.0 Agent Backend and Local sandbox images. (#44152)
  5. Preserve password hashing configuration. Existing installations without a pepper should leave PASSWORD_PEPPER empty. Setting a new pepper during the upgrade is not a transparent migration and requires an explicit password-reset plan. Keep any configured pepper unchanged across all instances and restore it with the database.
  6. Review the proxy boundary. Bundled Nginx replaces X-Forwarded-For with its resolved client address, and Compose enables forwarded-header handling. Keep direct API access restricted to trusted callers. If a load balancer or Cloudflare sits before Nginx, configure trusted real-IP handling there; otherwise visitors may share the proxy’s rate-limit bucket. See client IP and trusted proxies.
  7. Enable KnowledgeFS deliberately. Default Compose installations keep it off; local Community Edition development requires the explicit Community development opt-in. Configure its separate database and migrations, Capability v2 public verifier, Dify signing keys, model profile (embedding, reasoning, and rerank), and Workspace cutover gates before enabling traffic. The optional service must pass /ready, not only /health. Standard Dify API images do not contain the separate KnowledgeFS engine used by the optional engine-worker profile; the published default KnowledgeFS API image is currently amd64 only. Follow the KnowledgeFS deployment and recovery guide.
Deployment instructions · Docker Compose, source, and difyctl

Docker Compose

Once the 1.18.0 release images and tag are published, stop the old stack gracefully, switch to the release, merge the configuration changes above, and pull/start the new stack:

cd dify/docker
docker compose stop -t -1
git fetch --tags
git checkout 1.18.0
# Merge required configuration changes into existing env files here.
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Keep database migrations enabled (MIGRATION_ENABLED=true) for the API startup, or run them through your managed migration process before starting new workers. The bundled Weaviate update from 1.17.1 is a patch update within 1.39. If coming from a version that still runs Weaviate 1.27, complete the 1.17.1 staged Weaviate upgrade first.

Source Deployments

Use Python 3.13 for the API, Node.js 24.22.1 or later in the 24.x line, and pnpm 12.10.1. Refresh the locked dependencies and apply the database migrations from the repository root:

uv sync --project api --frozen
uv run --directory api flask db upgrade
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

Rebuild the web application and restart API, worker, scheduler, and Agent services from the same release. If deploying Agent Backend separately from source, refresh its locked server dependencies as well.

difyctl

Install the matching 1.18.0 client. Its v2 implementation does not reuse v1 login state:

difyctl login --server https://your-dify.example.com
difyctl help

Update scripts to the current server-discovered command surface. The old mode-agnostic /openapi/v1/apps/{app_id}:run route is replaced by per-mode operations; use the catalog instead of hard-coded v1 routes. Refresh installed agent skills with difyctl install skills <dir>. (#42487, #42608, #43819)

Existing data that may need recovery
  • Published triggers: the draft-sync fix does not repair subscriptions already removed before upgrading. Rebind missing subscriptions and republish affected workflows as needed. (#44068)
  • Document extraction: re-import/re-index affected content to apply extraction fixes to existing documents.
  • Built-in document metadata: toggling built-in fields rewrites only enabled, non-archived documents whose indexing is complete. Other legacy rows can retain the old format and need a later rewrite when eligible; this release does not include a full backfill. (#44218)

Detailed changes

New features · complete capabilities and availability

Agent Knowledge Base and KnowledgeFS

  • Add the Beta knowledge-space experience with local upload preview, connected-source management, document availability and metadata, retrieval history/research, and quality evaluation. Settings control app, Agent, and Service API access. Classic Knowledge remains supported alongside it. (#44165)
  • Knowledge Retrieval v2 and Agent knowledge bindings use scoped capabilities; published Explore runs reuse published bindings without requiring ordinary viewers to reconfigure access. (#44165)
  • Classic Dataset upgrades have durable checkpoints, availability/metadata reconciliation, retry protection, and recovery through Beat. Run the dedicated upgrade worker with the documented prefork pool and task limits; apply b9d3f7a5c102 before restarting API/workers/Beat. Opting into the service does not automatically migrate all Classic datasets. (#44165)

Portable App Packages

  • App exports now default to .ifpkg, bringing the application configuration and its supported resources into one portable package. Explicit YAML export remains available, and imports accept both formats from files or URLs. (#42066, #42189, #42425, #42552)
  • Workflow and Chatflow packages include inline Agents, their Skills, and files from each node’s bound configuration snapshot. Imports recreate those Agents in the destination workspace and remap their resources. App icons, Site settings, and node plugin dependencies are included in the export flow. Missing resources are reported during import. (#42579, #42626, #42816, #42863, #42913)
  • Agent exports can target a published version. Agent version menus now offer Restore, and pending draft saves finish before restoration so autosave cannot overwrite the restored configuration. Skill duplication and export use the latest saved draft content. (#42485, #42567, #42424, #42502)

Nested Workflow Tools and Trace Drilldown

  • Called Workflow Tools run as child graphs under the workflow engine, with coordinated pause, resume, stop, and file outputs. Source graphs are captured before execution, so republishing a tool does not change an in-flight run, including calls inside loops and iterations. (#40277, #42820)
  • Workflow, Chatflow, and history views can open a particular tool invocation and navigate its internal execution traces. Access to each source application is required before its details are returned. Human Input forms are tracked by execution identity, including repeated invocations of the same node. (#42819, #42821, #42822)
  • Nested Agent logs and usage records retain their source workflow identity and their relationship to the outer run. Nested usage and step totals can still be approximate, particularly after pauses or stops. (#42824, #42820)

Agent Output Routes and Streaming

  • Agent v2 nodes can select a workflow branch as part of completing their task. Enable Output Routes, define at least two branches and their selection conditions, and use the read-only switch output to inspect the chosen route. With routing disabled, the normal success outlet remains available. Routed nodes support stopping on error or taking a failure branch; node-level default-value handling is unavailable with routes enabled. (#42599)
  • Plain Agent v2 nodes stream text as it is generated. Structured or routed results remain buffered, and nodes using default-value error handling stay buffered so the configured fallback can still replace a failed result. (#43986)

Build and Manage Apps with OpenAPI and difyctl

  • /openapi/v1 publishes a server operation catalog. difyctl discovers commands and their input fields from that catalog, provides searchable help, and follows server-provided next steps. Workflow and Chatflow authoring now covers app creation, DSL import/export, settings, environment variables, publishing, and version restoration. Draft hashes protect imports from overwriting concurrent edits. (#42487, #42608, #43067)
  • The CLI includes a difyctl skill for agents building Dify apps. Install it with difyctl install skills <dir>. Device login supports --no-wait and --resume, and folder uploads send one multipart part per file. (#43819, #44356)
  • Workspace owners can create resource access tokens bound to selected apps or knowledge bases. Tokens work with the supported Service API routes and app operations in difyctl; they do not grant workspace administration. The Settings entry is opt-in through NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ACCESS_TOKEN, which defaults to false. (#42293, #44422)

Edit Agent Prompts from the Sandbox

  • dify-agent config prompt pull [--to PATH] and push [PATH|-] read or replace the raw system prompt, preserving UTF-8, whitespace, and mention markers. Empty text clears it. Only the current account’s writable build draft can be changed; later requests use the saved prompt. (#44561)

Agent Execution Tracing

  • Agent apps and Workflow Agent v2 nodes can export their Agent, model, and tool execution trees through the existing tracing providers. Monitoring adds shared tracing configuration, delivery status, retry controls, and links to the trace belonging to the selected execution. Agents referenced by a Workflow inherit the caller’s tracing policy. (#44144, #44186)
  • Application tracing is opt-in on both the API and Agent Backend. A separate deployment-wide OTLP trajectory exporter is also available, independently of system tracing. (#42651, #44144)
  • Called Workflow Tools’ internal nodes are excluded from external exports because those exports have no viewer identity for source-app access checks. Agents inside those called tools are also excluded from the new execution-tree export for now; authorized Console drilldown remains available. (#42823, #44144)

OpenShell Sandbox Backend and E2B Usage Collection

  • Agent execution can use a self-hosted NVIDIA OpenShell gateway with DIFY_AGENT_RUNTIME_BACKEND=openshell. Each Binding has its own sandbox, with authenticated shell access, Home Snapshots on an operator-managed shared volume, and an optional egress allowlist. OpenShell gateway 0.0.106 or newer and a compatible runtime image are required. (#41076)
  • OpenShell lease release closes the connection but leaves the sandbox running. There is no automatic idle-stop or sandbox TTL; operators must manage those resources. Multi-tenant deployments require separate OpenShell workspaces and snapshot volumes per tenant. See the OpenShell deployment guide.
  • Optional E2B usage collection records provider execution duration and resource sizes through Celery Beat and the ops_trace queue. Collection starts from a configured activation time and does not backfill earlier executions. Both the API and Agent Backend metering flags default to off. (#42554)

Cloud Access Controls, Templates, and Archive Management

  • Reusable network access groups let supported Cloud deployments share IP rules across apps, with permission checks, effective-policy status, and trusted client-IP previews. Enforcement depends on the Cloud policy service and Gateway; this is not a standalone Community Edition firewall. (#41025, #44464)
  • Cloud users can preview and try published Agent templates before importing them. Agent “Create from Template” is hidden in Community and Enterprise editions because its template data source is Cloud-only. (#42837, #44035)
  • In Cloud Workflow Log Archives, workspace owners can permanently delete a selected month, with confirmation, progress, and retry. The action removes archived objects and prepared ZIP downloads; live workflow-run records are outside its scope. Failed deletion jobs now enter the retry policy instead of reporting success. (#44052, #44061, #44203)
Improvements · performance, navigation, accessibility, and operations
  • Knowledge performance: dataset lists and indexing status use batched queries; segment imports avoid repeated position queries; retrieval and result post-processing reduce repeated lookups. (#42279, #42191, #42233, #42673, #43665)
  • Faster loading: translations load by feature, workflow configuration panels load on demand, and chart, music, and SVG previews defer heavier work. Chat history no longer loads saved prompts that are not needed for display. (#42812, #42873, #42874, #42877, #42970, #42840, #42951, #44521)
  • Navigation and accessibility: improved command discovery, keyboard navigation, focus return, dialog labels, and responsive layouts across Studio, workflow editing, Knowledge, Agent configuration, and workspace settings. Studio filters survive navigation, timezones are searchable, and workflow image export has a dedicated toolbar action. (#43133, #44330, #44429, #43944, #43662, #44220, #44378, #44492, #44535, #44539, #44548, #44564)
  • Floating controls: menus, selectors, popovers, and tooltips now use Base UI positioning directly, with migrated alignment and offset settings throughout the console. (#44588)
  • Date, time, and icons: redesigned date/time pickers, native scrolling for time options, and an updated icon picker with image cropping and self-hosted emoji assets. (#43090, #43723, #43007, #42469)
  • Localization: Azerbaijani (az-AZ) joins the supported UI languages, with additional translation and right-to-left layout improvements. (#42291, #43808)
  • Developer tooling: faster TypeScript checks through tsrs, plus typed Document and CustomizedSnippet models that preserve existing constructors and database defaults. (#44562, #36084, #40818)
  • Operations: archive storage supports configurable S3 addressing style; the API image includes its spaCy model so startup does not need to download it; workflow generation logs identify tools omitted from the bounded fallback catalog. (#43066, #43601, #42596)
Security enhancements
